extracted.intended_audience: readers of entertainment news, comedians, festival organisers and industry professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Stand-up/live comedy content evaluation in the context of festival/venue programming decisions, weighing artistic intent, audience reaction, and venue values. Focuses on what venues consider acceptable or unacceptable onstage language and acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue inclusivity and diversity policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance: Our values are to be inclusive, diverse and welcoming; we are proud of progress across programming including investment and support for Black, Asian and Global Majority artists, LGBTQ+ voices, those from working class backgrounds, and strong representation of women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venues that adopt explicit inclusivity/diversity goals will program and support underrepresented artists and consider those commitments when assessing whether content aligns with their remit. Programming decisions should reflect those stated priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: No content that attacks people's dignity
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance: We do not believe that racism, homophobia, sexism or misogynistic language have a place in our venues; we will not associate with content which attacks people’s dignity and the language used on stage was, in our view, completely unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material that is judged to attack the dignity of protected groups (racist, homophobic, sexist, misogynistic language) is considered unacceptable and can justify removal/cancellation regardless of performer intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolving standards: challenge older material
rubrics_metrics.description: In a changing world, stories and language that were once accepted on stage, whether performed in character or not, need to be challenged. There is a line that we will not cross at the Pleasance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptability of material is not static — acts once tolerated may now be judged unacceptable. Programmers should reassess legacy material against contemporary community standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience response as a signal (walkouts and complaints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasance cited 'numerous complaints' and reported walkouts and alleged 'abuse of staff' as a reason for cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial negative audience reaction (multiple walkouts, many complaints, reported staff abuse) is treated as evidence of misalignment with venue standards and can prompt immediate action such as cancelling performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic intent and thoughtful craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Performer defence: 'a lot of thought goes into my shows' and material can be 'funny, sometimes important and worth saying.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations may consider performer intent, craft and whether material aims to make a point or provoke thoughtful laughter rather than merely insult. Thoughtful intent can be cited in defence, though it may not override venue policy or audience harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provocation must serve a comedic purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Performer acknowledged exposing genitals but argued such acts are 'for the purpose of the funny line which follows it' — part of 'silly, exaggerated irony and nonsense.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit or shocking onstage actions are more defensible if they demonstrably serve a comedic or narrative purpose; gratuitous provocation is more likely to be judged unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor must be funny — shock alone is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Critic’s view: a comedian 'fails the most important test for a comic, he’s just not funny and no amount of shock will elevate his hacky material.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary metric for comedy is whether it elicits laughter; reliance solely on shock or transgression does not excuse weak writing or delivery and is criticized as insufficient artistic justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualization of offensive material (character/satire)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterargument (Richard Herring): complaining about offensive performance is like asking an actor who plays Macbeth to be arrested for murder — implying that performance context (character, satire) matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether offensive material is presented as part of a character, satire, or social critique; context can change interpretation, but contextualization does not automatically negate harm or venue policy concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing free speech and community standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension noted between claims of championing free speech and removing acts that violate values; venues assert both commitments while making programming decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venues must balance commitments to artistic freedom with their duty to uphold stated community values; this balance informs whether controversial material is allowed or removed and may lead to perceived contradictions.
